items.feature: Site-wide security review (authentication, authorization, role escalation, server-side permissions, input validation, XSS, SQL injection, CSRF, file uploads, path traversal, session handling, secrets, API endpoints, private grievance data, admin routes, security headers, rate limiting) with fixes, not just findings
items.notes: Full review, 2026-09-15. Most categories were already solid and are noted as verified, not re-implemented: authorization (every one of ~140 admin page.tsx/actions.ts files independently calls requireUser/requirePermission — verified by a script splitting every actions.ts on its exported-function boundaries and checking each one's own body, not just that the file contains the string somewhere); role assignment validates the target role against a fixed enum and is itself gated on users:manage, with no client-trusted role/permission ever accepted (the session cookie is an opaque random token, resolved from the database on every request — src/lib/auth/session.ts); SQL injection (Prisma is parameterized everywhere; the only raw query is `SELECT 1` in the health check, no interpolation); XSS (React auto-escapes everywhere; the one dangerouslySetInnerHTML — JSON-LD — already `<`-escapes, src/lib/seo.ts); CSRF (Next.js Server Actions verify Origin against Host automatically; no custom mutating Route Handlers exist, only GET file-serving/health routes); path traversal (every stored-file read already resolves and checks containment against its storage root, and every path segment comes from a DB-generated id or a randomUUID-prefixed sanitized filename, never raw user input); secrets (.env is gitignored, .env.example has no real values, GRIEVANCE_ENCRYPTION_KEY/DATABASE_URL are validated for presence/format in src/lib/env.ts, dev-seed credentials are never seeded when NODE_ENV=production); private grievance data (encrypted at rest, decrypted only on the permission-gated detail view, and the list query — while it does fetch the encrypted columns via Prisma's default `include` behavior — never renders them, verified by inspecting its DataTable columns). Real gaps found and fixed: (1) Login had per-account lockout but no per-IP rate limit, so an attacker could spread guesses across many different accounts from one source without ever tripping any single account's lockout — added the same RateLimitEntry-backed limiter the grievance form already used (see auth-login-rate-limit above). (2) File uploads (Document/Media/grievance attachments) validated only the client-asserted `File.type`, never the actual bytes — a scripted client can set any Content-Type on a multipart part it likes, so a disguised HTML/script file could be uploaded under an allow-listed MIME type and, for the inline-served Media route, risk a content-sniffing stored-XSS if a browser ever ignored the declared Content-Type. Added src/lib/security/file-signature.ts (magic-byte verification for every allow-listed type with a real signature — PDF/JPEG/PNG/GIF/WEBP/the legacy OLE2 Office formats/the ZIP-based OOXML formats) wired into both saveUploadedFile and saveGrievanceAttachment, so a mismatch is rejected before anything touches disk; tests/unit/security/file-signature.test.ts covers every type's accept/reject case directly, and the existing upload-storage/file-storage unit tests' fixtures were upgraded from placeholder text content to genuine magic-byte content they'd been implicitly relying on being irrelevant. (3) next.config.ts had zero security headers — added Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self', explicit allow-lists per resource type, object-src/frame-ancestors 'none', no external origins since the app loads no third-party scripts/fonts/images), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy, a locked-down Permissions-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security (production only), and poweredByHeader: false — verified present on a real `next start` response via curl, not just assumed from config. Known architectural gap, deliberately flagged rather than fixed: nearly every admin query filters records by `id` alone, not also by the signed-in user's `collegeId` — a real horizontal-authorization (IDOR) gap *if* this app ever became genuinely multi-tenant, but there is currently no code path anywhere that creates a second College row (verified: no prisma.college.create call exists, and the live dev database has exactly one), so today there is no other tenant's data to leak. Whether this app is single-tenant or a multi-tenant template is an explicit, still-open question (see progress.md); retrofitting collegeId scoping across ~30 modules' queries for a not-yet-decided requirement was judged out of scope for this review — see the decisions log. tsc/eslint clean; full 637/637 unit + full e2e regression (211/212 — the one failure is the same pre-existing, already-documented test-data-accumulation flake from shell-accessibility-audit's session, unrelated to any change here) re-run after every fix; a real `next start` production build was started and its response headers verified directly.

items.feature: Fixed two Playwright cross-file concurrency bugs found while running the first-ever full 250-test e2e regression (the same command the new CI pipeline runs), so the suite passes reliably as a whole rather than only in hand-picked subsets
items.notes: 2026-09-17. (1) tests/e2e/admin-governance.spec.ts's role-edit test granted audit_logs:view to EDITOR to prove a live grant takes effect, but tests/e2e/dashboard.spec.ts and tests/e2e/audit-logs.spec.ts both assert EDITOR's baseline lacks that permission, and Playwright runs different spec files concurrently (fullyParallel: true) — caused a real intermittent dashboard.spec.ts failure. Fixed by mutating FACULTY_EDITOR instead (grepped to confirm no other spec assumes a baseline for that role); re-ran the four colliding files together (46 tests) to confirm. (2) submitGrievance's rate limit (src/lib/security/rate-limit.ts) keys on a hash of x-forwarded-for/x-real-ip, which the local Playwright-driven dev server never sends (no real reverse proxy in front of `next dev`) — every test request hashed to the same "unknown" bucket, and three spec files (grievance.spec.ts, public-content.spec.ts, audit-logs.spec.ts) each perform one real grievance submission against a 3-per-hour limit, guaranteeing a collision on a full run. Not a production bug — Vercel reliably sets x-forwarded-for per real visitor. Fixed by giving each of those three files its own test.use({ extraHTTPHeaders: { "x-forwarded-for": "<distinct fake IP>" } }), simulating exactly what a real reverse proxy already provides in production; the rate-limit code itself was not touched (CLAUDE.md rule 10 — no test or security control was weakened, the test's simulated network topology was corrected to match reality). Verified with a full 250-test run: 249 passed, 1 unrelated pre-existing flake (mobile-viewport horizontal-overflow check under 5-worker CPU contention, passed cleanly in isolation, not chased further).

items.feature: Fixed a critical `next build` regression where the root layout's generateMetadata() required a live database connection to build at all, which would have broken every Vercel deploy
items.notes: 2026-09-17. Caught by deliberately re-running `npm run build` against a nonexistent placeholder DATABASE_URL (matching .github/workflows/ci.yml's build job exactly), not by trusting an earlier same-day build check that had unknowingly run against the real local dev DB. src/app/layout.tsx's generateMetadata() (added earlier the same day) called getPrimaryCollege() unguarded; the root layout's metadata resolves for every route, including ones Next statically prerenders at build time (/admin/*, /_not-found), unlike the homepage's own generateMetadata which is force-dynamic and only ever resolves at request time. Build failed hard with a PrismaClientKnownRequestError and a nonzero exit code -- exactly what the deployment skill's 'next build must never require a live external service' rule and the CI build job's own comment both warn against; every Vercel deploy would have failed. Fixed with `.catch(() => FALLBACK_SITE_NAME)` around the DB read in both layout.tsx and page.tsx's generateMetadata -- degrades to the same placeholder string already used for the 'no college row yet' case, now also covering 'DB unreachable', no fabricated data. Verified with the real failure-reproducing command (DATABASE_URL=<nonexistent-placeholder> npm run build) -- now exits 0. Re-ran the full 250-test e2e suite and all 672 unit tests against the real dev DB afterward to confirm the fallback doesn't mask or change real, DB-connected metadata output (homepage SEO/title e2e tests still assert the real college name). No dedicated unit test added for generateMetadata itself -- it isn't exercised anywhere in the existing suite (no file imports next/font/google, which layout.tsx pulls in, and there's no existing Vitest mock for it), and the real `next build` run against a genuinely absent database is a stronger, more direct verification of this exact failure mode than a mocked unit test would be.

items.feature: Real browser-automation walkthrough of the whole product — the public site's 10 main entry points and the full admin notice lifecycle (login → dashboard → create → draft → submit → review → approve → publish → verify publicly → edit → audit trail) plus a compliance-dashboard verification, at both desktop and a real 375×812 mobile viewport
items.notes: New tests/e2e/full-walkthrough.spec.ts (21 tests), run against the real dev server + seeded database with real browser interaction throughout — typing into the actual search box and clicking Search rather than navigating straight to `?q=`, following the real Edit link rather than calling a Server Action directly, etc. Found and fixed one real defect: at 375px width, the admin dashboard (`/admin`) overflowed horizontally. Root-caused by tracing computed widths up the DOM ancestor chain from the overflowing content rather than guessing — the "Recent notices"/"Upcoming events" cards sit in a `grid gap-6 lg:grid-cols-2` (single implicit column below `lg:`), and a CSS Grid item's default `min-width: auto` means it won't shrink below its content's intrinsic width unless told to; a long notice/event title inside a `flex items-center justify-between` row (with a `truncate` class the original author clearly intended to engage) never actually got the chance to truncate, because the *grid item* (the Card) itself, not just the text link, needed `min-w-0` to be allowed to shrink in the first place — a second, independent instance of the same flexbox/grid "intrinsic minimum size" trap already documented once in this project for the public header's nav (see the 2026-09-13 shell-responsive-no-horizontal-scroll decision). Fixed with `min-w-0` on both `<Card>`s (src/app/admin/page.tsx) plus `min-w-0 flex-1` on the two notice/event title `<Link>`s inside them (the latter alone was insufficient by itself — verified by measuring the DOM at each fix step rather than assuming one change was enough). Re-verified via direct `document.documentElement.scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` measurement (equal after the fix, previously 434 vs 375) as well as the full walkthrough spec passing end to end at 375px. tsc/eslint clean; full 637/637 unit + full e2e regression (232/233 — the one failure is the same pre-existing, already-documented test-data-accumulation flake, unrelated) re-run after the fix; a real production build (`npm run build`) verified clean.

cms_modules.description: CMS modules for College Profile, Departments, Programs, Faculty, Staff, Notices, Events, Seminars, Workshops, Academic Calendar, Timetables, Admissions, Fee Structures, Enrollment Statistics, Examinations, Results, Documents, Infrastructure, Activities, Clubs, Gallery, Scholarships, Student Support, Policies, Regulations, Affiliation, Contact, and Location — the first real admin-side content authoring in the project (everything before this was PagePlaceholder). Each module has list/view/create/edit pages plus the full content approval workflow (DRAFT -> SUBMITTED -> UNDER_REVIEW -> APPROVED -> PUBLISHED, and PUBLISHED -> UPDATE_REQUIRED -> DRAFT — see the cms-workflow-engine entry), sharing one generic engine (src/lib/content-workflow.ts) and one audit-log writer (src/lib/audit.ts) rather than reimplementing either 28 times. Notices/Events/Seminars/Workshops/Academic Calendar/Timetables/Admissions/Examinations/Results/Affiliation also share src/lib/admin/zod-helpers.ts for date-field validation/conversion. Admissions/Fee Structures/Enrollment Statistics are the first modules in the `content_admissions` domain and Examinations/Results the first in `content_examinations`; Clubs is the third `content_faculty` module (alongside Faculty/Staff). Documents closed the long-tracked Document publish-gate gap; this batch similarly added `publishedAt`/`publishedBy` to `Contact` and `Location`, which (like `FeeStructure`/`EnrollmentStatistic`/`Result` before them) had `status` but not the publish-timestamp columns the shared workflow engine needs. Gallery is the first nested-resource module (GalleryAlbum -> GalleryItem, where adding an item also creates a fresh Media asset in the same action) and Location is the second true singleton module (after College Profile), using `findFirst` rather than `findUnique` since `Location.collegeId` has no `@unique` constraint.

items.feature: Content approval workflow state machine: DRAFT -> SUBMITTED -> UNDER_REVIEW -> APPROVED -> PUBLISHED, and PUBLISHED -> UPDATE_REQUIRED -> DRAFT. Every transition enforces the caller's permission (manage for submit_for_review/return_to_draft, publish for start_review/approve/reject/publish/request_update), is refused if illegal from the record's current status, stores the actor + a timestamp + an optional comment/reason on the audit log entry it writes, and rejection specifically requires a non-empty reason. Only PUBLISHED content is ever publicly visible (src/lib/content.ts's `isPubliclyVisible` / status: "PUBLISHED" filters).
items.notes: tests/unit/content-workflow.test.ts — 32 tests covering every one of the 7 transitions (parameterized), illegal-transition rejection (WorkflowError), the rejection-requires-a-reason rule (empty and whitespace-only both refused), comment storage on both reject and non-reject transitions, publishedAt/publishedBy set only on publish, getAvailableActions' permission filtering for every status, and isPubliclyVisible. Superseded the prior DRAFT/PENDING_REVIEW/APPROVED/PUBLISHED/ARCHIVED engine via prisma/migrations/20260914150000_content_approval_workflow_v2 (applied against the real local Postgres instance with zero drift; no ARCHIVED/PENDING_REVIEW rows existed in seeded data, so the remap was a schema-only change in practice). items.notes: tests/unit/admin/enrollment-statistics/actions.test.ts. Found a real Zod pitfall while building this: `z.coerce.number().min(0).optional().or(z.literal(""))` silently turns a blank field into 0 rather than falling through to the empty-string branch, because `Number("") === 0` already satisfies `min(0)` before the literal("") alternative is ever tried (unlike the pre-existing establishedYear precedent, whose min(1800) bound reliably fails for a coerced-to-0 blank value) — fixed by passing `formData.get(x) || undefined` into a plain `.optional()` schema instead of routing a literal empty string through the number coercion at all. This is a CLAUDE.md rule 1 correctness fix (never invent data), not just a style choice.

admin_system.notes: Real, database-derived dashboard (src/app/admin/page.tsx + src/lib/admin/dashboard.ts) behind requirePermission("dashboard:view"). Summary cards: total published/draft/pending-review content (site-wide groupBy across all 28 content-authoring modules, summed only across modules the signed-in user holds :view on — never a site-wide leak to a narrowly-scoped role), compliance percentage (share of the 20 circular requirements actually VERIFIED by a human, not average completeness), requirements needing attention, and document expiry warnings. Tables: recent notices, upcoming events (both all-status, not just published — staff need to see their own pending work), compliance requirements needing attention (worst-status-first: NEEDS_UPDATE > READY_FOR_REVIEW > IN_PROGRESS > NOT_STARTED), content not recently reviewed (published content untouched for 180+ days, across the ~19 modules with an actual editorial title), document expiry warnings (expired or expiring within 30 days), and recent audit activity. Every section gated by the same permission its own admin module already enforces (compliance:view, audit_logs:view, content_general:view), so a role only ever sees real data for domains it can actually open — CLAUDE.md rule 5. No number is hard-coded; an empty database yields all zeros, never a fabricated placeholder value. Covered by tests/unit/admin/dashboard.test.ts (permission filtering, status aggregation, staleness threshold, compliance percent/priority ordering, expiry classification, audit actor fallback) and tests/e2e/dashboard.spec.ts (9 tests: per-role section visibility, live increments from real admin actions, and the full upload→publish→dashboard-expiry-warning path). Real per-record review tracking (src/lib/content-review.ts) for the 5 modules the task explicitly named warnings for — Notices, Faculty, Academic Calendar, Timetables, Admissions (Documents already has its own, more precise freshness signal, expiryDate, so it's out of scope here; the engine itself is generic and extending to more modules later is additive, not a redesign). Each record now has lastReviewedAt/lastReviewedById (prisma/migrations/20260917000000_content_review_tracking); every module's [id]/page.tsx shows a ReviewPanel (last updated, last reviewed, next review date, reviewer) plus a Mark reviewed action gated on the module's :publish permission (a higher-trust accuracy check, same tier as approve/publish) that writes a new MARK_REVIEWED audit entry via the centralized logAudit(). "Next review due" is always computed live as (lastReviewedAt ?? publishedAt ?? createdAt) + the module's configured period — never stored — so changing a period retroactively affects every record's overdue status immediately, no backfill needed. The review period is configurable per module at /admin/content-review-settings (new ReviewPeriodSetting table, one row per explicit override; DEFAULT_REVIEW_PERIOD_DAYS=180 for any module without one), gated behind compliance:verify (PRINCIPAL/ADMINISTRATOR/SUPER_ADMIN — reused rather than adding a new permission for one settings screen). The dashboard's new review-warnings section is covered under adm-dashboard above. Also found and fixed a real pre-existing bug while running the full e2e suite: getNotices()/getImportantAnnouncement() in src/lib/content.ts ordered by `publishDate desc` with no explicit NULLS handling — Postgres's default for DESC is NULLS FIRST, so any notice with no publishDate set always outranked every dated notice as "most current," regardless of actual recency. Fixed with explicit `nulls: "last"` on both queries.
